clue.text: Figure of speech to hamper 0 eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, telling us to rearrange the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric hampered by a turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' is the anagram signal: the eight letters of 'to hamper' rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a standard figure of speech, describing one thing in terms of another.

clue.text: Mum, starting holiday abroad, may have a seat on a jumbo

definitions.text: may have a seat on a jumbo

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: starting picks only the opening letter of the word holiday

parts.note: abroad can mean out and about, so out

explanation.surface: Mother goes abroad on holiday and rides an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' looks like a jet but is an elephant; the definition describes who sits on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is an elephant driver, who sits on the animal's neck.

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a tight spot is a dangerous or difficult one
to moor a boat is to rope it to the quay

explanation.surface: A man from the Moors holds up a risky circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' suggests a North African or open land; it is the verb to tie up a boat. In a down clue 'supporting' puts ROPE under TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking a high wire is a classic circus performance.

explanation.surface: A secure prison room.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang the word names both a strongbox that safecrackers blow and a prisoner's cell.

clue.text: Stroke, perhaps, as Roman gets in a mess

indicators.note: getting in a mess means the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Roman rower makes a hash of his stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' is the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The stroke is one example of a rower in an eight, setting the rhythm for the crew.

clue.text: Resolution of one into return journeys

indicators.note: into places the piece for one inside the other
return asks for the word for journeys to be read backwards

parts.note: trips are short journeys
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone finding resolve on round-trip journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, and 'into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is courage and determination, so a synonym for resolution.

clue.text: Uncontrolled firing in extremely panicky Black Sea state

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word panicky

parts.note: Romania is a country with a Black Sea coast

explanation.surface: Panic in a Black Sea country as guns go off at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests gunfire but means setting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to set fires, uncontrolled arson.

clue.text: Product of sap keeping son in check

indicators.note: keeping means the word for check holds the letter for son inside

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A father restrains a foolish son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sap' suggests a fool, but it is the plant fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky substance exuded by trees, made from their sap.

indicators.note: twist tells us to rearrange the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Praise for the dance song Twist and Shout.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title hides the mechanism: 'Twist' is the anagram signal on AND SHOUT. A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a sum of one thousand.

parts.note: meat that is smelling is said to be high
old salts and tars are both slang for sailors

explanation.surface: Smelling salts kept at naval headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelling-salts' reads as one remedy but splits into two pieces. Admirals are the top-ranking sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiralty is the body of the most senior naval officers, the top-ranking seamen.

explanation.surface: A self-proclaimed fast talker in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift called himself Presto in his Journal to Stella. 'bars' are musical measures, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the nickname the satirist Jonathan Swift used for himself, and in a musical score it is the marking for a very fast tempo.

indicators.note: enough of the two words is taken to give a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A cricket captain with plenty of runs closes the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of declaring an innings misleads; the answer runs across 'hAVE Runs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or state firmly.

explanation.surface: An ideal condition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or absolute, as in a perfect stranger; as a verb it means to say or speak.

explanation.surface: Changes in the parts of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Moves or trends in events are developments, and a symphony is divided into separate musical parts of the same name.

indicators.note: in places the word for states inside the word for change

parts.note: coins are loose change
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A family member talks about small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like a verb but is the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle.

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The best-suited building material is partly steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' is the anagram signal on SEMISTEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper or suitable, so the superlative is the most appropriate.

parts.note: to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them
corn is cereal grain

explanation.surface: Grain being smuggled into Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNCORN is an industrial town in Cheshire, a county of north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The place named is a town in that county, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Toy breeds running wild in home for the rest of the natives

definitions.text: home for the rest of the natives

indicators.note: running wild means the letters of the words before it are scattered and re-formed

explanation.surface: Toy dog breeds going feral in a home for local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natives' are native oysters, a name for British-farmed ones, not local people.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are a variety of shellfish, and their bed is where they live and lie at rest.

clue.text: Lines confessing he is a poet

parts.note: BR is British Rail, a crossword stand-in for railway lines
owning up is confessing

explanation.surface: A poet confesses his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests verse; it is the railway. Robert Browning was a Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote dramatic monologues such as My Last Duchess.

definitions.meaning: naval slang gave junior officers this name because they reefed sails; plural

explanation.surface: Young naval officers rolling cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Midshipmen were called this in old naval slang, and it is also slang for cannabis cigarettes.

explanation.surface: A famous ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone praised in song is celebrated, and the Chinese ruling house of 960 to 1279 bears this name.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to raise someone is to promote them

explanation.surface: A bishop gives the cook a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is a verb here, not the kitchen worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is a way to cook slowly in a covered pot.

clue.text: Type with relative turning up in small restaurants

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
sib is short for sibling, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member arrives with a printer's type at a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SORTSIB as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistros are modest French-style eating places.

explanation.surface: The carer of a US composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a child not one's own is to bring it up, and Stephen Foster wrote Oh! Susanna.

clue.text: Wellingtons, for example, twist out of shape on country roads

parts.note: to warp is to bend out of shape
lanes are narrow rural roads

explanation.surface: Rubber boots get bent out of shape on muddy lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellingtons' suggests rubber boots, but the Vickers Wellington was a Second World War bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wellington was a British bomber aircraft, one example of a military plane.

clue.text: Travelled with nothing on to see cowboys' display

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Riding with no clothes on to watch a cowboy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of riding and roping skills by cowboys.

indicators.note: in places the colour inside the abbreviation for a firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
cardinal is a deep red colour

explanation.surface: A churchman holds strong religious conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, a creed.

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first pieces above the next

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, and two firms merging give two of them
the second of the two merged companies, another Co

explanation.surface: Companies agree a merger over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merge' tells us to join two copies of CO, set 'over' A in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink.

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A trendy act, without doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphasis meaning truly or certainly.

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, good-hearted person
a bat is a batsman

explanation.surface: Harsh words about a dependable teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brick' is old British slang for a dependable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a harsh remark, from a lump of brick thrown as a missile.

clue.text: This artist got it right with a circle

indicators.note: to put right is to set in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: An artist proves himself by drawing a perfect circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the story that Giotto proved his skill by drawing a perfect circle freehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto was an early Italian Renaissance painter.
